Bring Your Own Power: Behind-the-Meter Power Projects for Data Centers

Grid interconnection queues now stretch three to seven years in many U.S. markets — far longer than the 18 to 24 months it takes to build a data center. To close that gap, developers are increasingly building power on their own side of the meter: gas turbines and reciprocating engines, fuel cells, and battery energy storage system (BESS)- backed microgrids sited next to the facilities they serve. Nearly 90 GW of behind-the-meter (BTM) gas-fired capacity — turbines and reciprocating engines — has been announced in the U.S. alone, and on-site or hybrid generation now accounts for close to half of all newly announced data center capacity.
This shift changes what “power reliability” means for a data center.
